news.title: SWNT assistant Leanne Ross tells girls to 'dream big' as home World Cup confirmed
news.lede: Glasgow City head coach Leanne Ross is also Melissa Andreatta's SWNT assistant. Scotland assistant Leanne Ross believes having the Women's World Cup on home soil in 2035 can inspire the next generation of female players to "dream big". England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the showpiece tournament in nine years' time. "Dream it, go and do it, grab it with both hands," Ross said.

news.title: Limerick Teenager With Famous Name Inspired Brilliant Ireland U17s World Cup Win
news.lede: The Ireland U17s picked up their first victory of the 2026 World Cup in Qatar, as they deservedly ran out 2-0 winners against Costa Rica on Tuesday afternoon. At the centre of it all was a man with a very familiar name, Limerick native Cillian Murphy, fresh off the back of a breakthrough season with Cork City that has drawn interest from some of the continent's biggest clubs. Ireland's U17s World Cup opener against the might of Brazil ended in heartbreak on Saturday, with Eduardo Conceição netting the winner with less than 20 minutes to play. Recommended The Irish youngsters came storming out of the blocks on Tuesday afternoon, knowing a win here was pivotal to their hopes of progressing to the round of 32.

news.title: Jamaica joins US, Mexico and Costa Rica in landmark 2031 World Cup hosting role
news.lede: Jamaica has secured a landmark place in international football history, becoming part of a four-nation partnership to host the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup and paving the way for the Reggae Girlz to automatically qualify for the expanded 48-team tournament. The announcement, confirmed by FIFA President Gianni Infantino at the organization's Congress in Zurich, Switzerland, on Monday, places Jamaica alongside the United States, Mexico and Costa Rica as co-hosts of the global showpiece. The historic achievement marks the first time a Caribbean nation will host matches at a senior FIFA World Cup, opening an unprecedented opportunity for Jamaica to showcase its football infrastructure, sporting ambitions, culture and hospitality to a worldwide audience.

news.title: Donald Trump celebrates as US named co-host of 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup | Football News
news.lede: United States President Donald Trump celebrated on Tuesday as FIFA named the nation as co-host for the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup, alongside Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. This will be a third consecutive FIFA tournament where the United States play hosts after the Club World Cup in 2025 and the men's World Cup in 2026. Taking to a post on Truth Social, Trump backed the tournament’s expected economic impact and said it would showcase "America’s Exceptionalism"." After hosting the Most Successful World Cup in History, no Country is better positioned than the United States to be home to the largest Women's Sporting Event in History," he wrote.

news.title: Nigeria in the Quagmire of Being Unable to Host World Cup - Infantino
news.lede: Nigeria, 24 November 2026 - Nigeria, 23 November 2026 – FIFA President Gianni Infantino has spoken a bitter truth to Nigerian authorities, especially those responsible for ensuring that the country has state-of-the-art sports infrastructure, along with supportive and related infrastructure, that meets recommended international standards. He told ARISE News in Abuja that Nigeria, as it stands now, could not host a FIFA World Cup. "Today, no," Infantino said during the interview, in which he went further to cite inadequate infrastructure as the reason. Infantino is himself a man under siege.

news.title: Home World Cup can inspire Wales' future stars
news.lede: Rhian Wilkinson was appointed Wales head coach in February 2024. Wales head coach Rhian Wilkinson says the prospect of a home Women's World Cup in 2035 can inspire a generation of young Welsh players. The Football Association of Wales (FAW) launched its new women's and girls' 10-year football strategy on Tuesday, less than 24 hours after Wales - along with England, Scotland and Northern Ireland - were confirmed as co-hosts of the 2035 Women's World Cup. Cardiff and Wrexham are both proposed host cities.
